question: A city tracked the total number of streetlights installed downtown throughout the renovation, starting with 187 streetlights already up. A dozen crews worked the project, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked light count. A first phase added 42 more streetlights. A second phase added 69 more. A citywide expansion multiplied the tracked count by 7. A grant-funded extension doubled the tracked count once more. A separate suburb, unrelated to this project, installed 500 streetlights. Finally, an audit found 1943 streetlights had been double-counted and removed them from the tracked total. How many streetlights did the tracked downtown count show after the audit?

On Saturday morning a tennis club found 22 balls in the ball basket, and half of them were too worn to use and were thrown away. Before lunch a member donated 66 new balls to the basket. In the afternoon the coach added 12 balls he had in his car. That evening a supplier delivered 41 more. How many balls are in the basket now?
Emma had 44 dollars. She added 29, spent 41, gained 44, spent 18, earned 56, and spent 30. A store had a dozen items separately. How much remained?

A candy shop starts the day with 232 lollipops on display. A school field trip buys up 116 of them within the first hour. A birthday party order then takes another 60 lollipops off the shelf. A clumsy display mishap costs the shop 24 more lollipops that shatter and can't be sold. At closing, the shop owner sets aside half of what remains for tomorrow's display, and the story follows only that half from here. A morning delivery the next day adds 32 more lollipops to that batch. How many lollipops does that batch have now?
A farm starts with 110 animals. It loses 48 (62). It loses 20 (42). It multiplies by 6 (252). It multiplies by 3 (756). It adds 31 (787). Double of 18 is 36. Bbb has 500. How many animals?

A company had 218 items initially. They multiplied by 2 for distribution. They multiplied by 6 for storage. They added 71 more items. They multiplied by 2 for packaging. They divided by 2 for shipping. The warehouse was 3000 square feet. How many items shipped?

Sara and Diego build model bridges at their engineering club. Sara's box held 58 wooden rods to start with, she bought 50 more from the craft shop, and Diego handed her 60, which was more than she had bought herself. Each rod in the box can be cut into 5 short pegs for the joints. The club then packed all the pegs equally into 4 storage boxes. The club's inventory is written up in single pegs rather than in full boxes. How many pegs are in one storage box?
Two colleagues compared. One had 132 hours. Halved morning. Lost 54. Added 65. Multiplied by 4. By 6 weekly. Converting to workdays, how many?

Liam had $232 saved toward a new guitar, while his brother Kai had $150 saved for a drum set. A summer job bonus turned every dollar Liam had into 2 dollars. A holiday bonus then turned every dollar into 3 dollars, a payout that took '60 minutes, or one hour' to process at the bank. He then received $4 more from a birthday card. A final matching program turned every dollar into 3 dollars. How much money did Liam have after the final matching program?

A warehouse had 225 boxes. They doubled to 450. They multiplied by 4 to 1,800. They added 13, reaching 1,813. They added 25 more, reaching 1,838. They removed 406, leaving 1,432 boxes. How many boxes remain?

A dairy farm started the morning with 230 liters of milk collected. By midmorning, 36 more liters came in from a second herd, and the stock was then multiplied across 6 identical tanks, each holding that same amount, for the co-op pickup. In the afternoon, 46 more liters were added from a late delivery. Since the farm measures milk in liters but the co-op invoice lists gallons, the farmer always double-checked the conversion before selling. A regional order required 8 times that afternoon total. By evening, 7978 liters had to be set aside for a separate processing plant. How many liters were left for the co-op after that?

A theatre started its run with 217 programmes, of which 48 were handed to the cast on opening night. The printer then delivered 78 extra programmes. For the tour the company ordered 3 programmes for every one it was holding. Over the tour 693 programmes were sold. The remainder was shared equally between the company's 2 storerooms, and the north storeroom's share was set aside for the archive. The box office quotes running times in minutes although the posters give them in hours. How many programmes went into the archive?

A town had 19 parks. They added 68 through new construction. They added 36 more. They multiplied by 9 for master planning. They added 70 final parks. A nearby city had 500 parks but unrelated. After both additions but before the multiplication, how many parks did the town have?

A student had 157 dollars (morning). They subtracted 12 for supplies. They added 47 from work. They added 13 bonus (afternoon). They subtracted 37 for purchase. They added 26 back (from refund). They subtracted 97 for major expense. Using 'double' as a word quantity and 'one distractor' (a scholarship of 500 dollars). After supplies and work earnings but before bonus, how much in the intermediate?

A charity cycle shop had 177 helmets on the racks and sold 65 of them at the summer sale. A donor returned 7 that had never been worn. The manager, Bea, sent 52 helmets to a partner project run by Otto, whose shop keeps fewer helmets than Bea's does. A school then donated 28 helmets to the shop. A dozen bicycles stood chained outside the door. The shop's price list is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many helmets does the shop have?

Sarah began the month with 217 dollars. She earned 46 dollars from tutoring. She then spent 143 dollars on supplies. Later she found 19 dollars. Finally she earned 28 dollars from freelance work. Her brother had 600 dollars but that's not relevant. How much money does Sarah have now?

A charity walk began with 58 dollars pledged at sign-up, while a separate fun run nearby collected 500 water bottles for its own runners, unrelated to this event. During the walk, 46 dollars had to be refunded to a canceled participant. A bake sale table added 3 more dollars, and a raffle added 20 more dollars. A matching gift added 6 more dollars. A late donor added 39 more dollars. A final pledge added 69 more dollars. How much money had the walk raised in total?

Kaia sets more climbing holds than her colleague Ben does. The store held 177 holds, and 127 of them were bolted onto the new wall. A supplier then delivered 53 holds to the same store. A sponsor doubled the number of holds in the store. Ben added 8 holds he had been keeping in his van. How many holds are in the store now?

A school received 12 tins of paint, and every tin was decanted into 3 glass jars. The jars were shared equally between 2 art rooms, and the upstairs room took one of those shares. A mural that covers 9 square metres used up 12 jars from the upstairs room. The jars still left there were divided equally among the 3 classes that use the room, and Class B took one share. Class B split its jars equally between 2 project groups, and the model-making group received one of the parts. The model-making group's cupboard already held 68 jars of paint. How many jars did the model-making group then have?

In the morning Sam started selling from a roll of 152 raffle tickets, and by noon he had sold 131 of them. In the afternoon 15 tickets got wet and were thrown away, and 3 more were torn. The organiser then let him swap each remaining ticket for 2 new ones, and gave him 44 loose tickets as well. In the evening Sam sold every ticket he had for 5 dollars each. How many dollars did Sam collect in the evening?

A warehouse operates through three shifts. They start with 55 items. In the morning, they divide by 5 for five receiving zones. They multiply by 6 for six distribution routes. They multiply by 5 to scale across five days. They multiply by 7 to project weekly. They add 12 items from corrections. The facility has 11 workers. How many items per week are projected?

A teacher plans her curriculum starting with 163 minutes of core instruction. She adds 17 minutes for supplementary activities. She adds 9 minutes for reflection. She then multiplies her time by 4 to plan for four weeks of lessons. She multiplies by 8 again to plan for two months. How many hours of total instructional time does she need?

The Lyric theatre has 171 seats, but 27 of them are blocked off for the lighting rig during the festival. The theatre runs 6 shows a day, and on top of the seats it sells 21 standing tickets each day. A ticket costs 30 dollars. The festival lasts 5 days, and every seat and standing ticket was sold for every show, which pleased the theatre's dozen volunteers. How many tickets were sold during the festival?

A server hosting company starts the month with 55 gigabytes of data backed up. A client migration multiplies the backup by 9. A second migration multiplies it by 6. A third multiplies it by 5. A fourth multiplies it by 7, a transfer that takes 180 minutes, or three hours. Finally, 12 more gigabytes are added from a manual upload. How many gigabytes of data are backed up now?

In the morning, a warehouse had 153 boxes. By midday, they received 7 times as many. In the afternoon, the count increased 6 times. By evening, it increased 6 times again. That night, 20 more boxes arrived. The next morning, 70 more boxes were added. How many boxes are in the warehouse?
